transcript.text: Our Dyson (one of the V ones, purple bits) keeps cutting out after about 5-10 seconds. Not every time - some days it does a whole room fine. It's maybe 5 years old. Already cleaned the filter and checked for blockages. Battery or something else?

To answer your question: yes, a battery is the most likely culprit given the age and intermittent nature of the fault. Dyson batteries typically last 3–5 years; after that, they lose capacity and may cut out under load even if they show charge. However, before replacing it, we need to rule out a charging issue or confirm the runtime. Please check two things:
1. When you place it on the charger, does the light come on immediately? Does it stay solid while charging (usually 3–4 hours for a full charge)?
2. After a full charge, if you use it on normal mode (not boost/max), how many seconds or minutes does it run before cutting out? If the light never comes on when plugged in, check that the socket works and wipe the metal charging contacts on both the vacuum and the charger dock with a dry cloth. If the light stays solid but it still dies after 5–10 seconds even on normal mode, the battery is almost certainly worn out and needs replacement.

Charger light comes on and the plug goes in fine, and it shows full blue lights when charged. On normal mode it cuts out less often, but on Max it nearly always stops within a few seconds. Battery not swollen or hot, if that matters.

This suggests the battery is worn out. Dyson batteries typically last 3–5 years; after that, they lose their ability to hold a high current. The 'full blue lights' only show voltage at rest, not capacity under load. Max mode demands a huge surge of power which the degraded cells can't provide, so the vacuum cuts in immediately to protect itself. Normal mode draws less power, which is why it runs longer but still eventually fails. The fix is to replace the battery pack. You can buy a replacement battery from Dyson or a third-party retailer; just ensure it's compatible with your specific V-model (e.g., V6, V7, V8). Once replaced, the Max mode should work normally again.
